topic: Current topic: is personalized news good for us? Many news apps, social platforms, and search engines now use algorithms to personalize the news people see, based on their past clicks, interests, and behavior. Aim: cover this topic in a way that makes both sides strongly true at once, not a simple good-vs-bad framing. On one side, personalization makes news consumption more convenient and relevant: it saves people time, surfaces stories that match their actual interests, and helps people cut through information overload. On the other side, personalization raises real concerns: filter bubbles (seeing mostly information that confirms existing views), worldview narrowing (a shrinking, self-reinforcing range of perspectives and topics over time), and editorial control shifting from human editors to opaque ranking algorithms with commercial incentives. Use only facts confirmed by web search (no invented details, no facts supplied from the assistant's own prior knowledge).

kept_facts.claim: Google News personalizes selected sections using user-specified interests and sources, plus past activity on Google services and YouTube.
kept_facts.subject: Google News personalization
kept_facts.scope: Google News users; specified personalized sections include For you, Following topics/sources/locations, Picks for you, local news, notifications, and the Android Audio Briefing
kept_facts.conditions: Personalization based on Web & App Activity depends on the user's activity settings.
kept_facts.source_title: How Google News stories are selected ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/googlenews/answer/9005749?hl=en&utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: State the product mechanism narrowly; do not generalize Google News settings to every news app or platform.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Google Newsの公式ヘルプは、ニュースのパーソナライズがGoogle Newsの設定（関心、フォローしたソース）と、GoogleサービスおよびYouTubeでの過去の活動に基づくと明記している。また、「For you」「Following」のトピック・ソース・地域、「Picks for you」、ローカルニュース、通知、Android版Audio Briefingを対象セクションとして列挙している。([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/googlenews/answer/9005749?hl=en))

kept_facts.claim: Google News provides user controls to follow or unfollow topics, locations, and sources; request more or fewer stories like a selected story; and hide all stories from a source.
kept_facts.subject: User control over news personalization
kept_facts.conditions: The customization feature is available when the user is signed in to a Google Account.
kept_facts.source_title: Customize what you find on Google News ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/googlenews/answer/9010862?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en&utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This supports the existence of user influence and opt-down controls; it does not show that users understand or routinely use them.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Google Newsの公式ヘルプは、Googleアカウントへのログインが必要であること、トピック・地域・ソースのフォロー／フォロー解除、特定記事について「より多く／少なく表示」、ソース全体の非表示が可能であることを直接説明している。([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/googlenews/answer/9010862?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en))

kept_facts.claim: Facebook describes its News Feed as a ranked system that uses signals such as who a person follows, likes, or recently engages with, and predicts the likelihood that the person will be interested in or engage with each post.
kept_facts.subject: Facebook Feed ranking
kept_facts.scope: Facebook News Feed; Meta's description of its ranking system
kept_facts.conditions: The ranking system operates on candidate posts available to each user and orders them by predicted relevance or engagement.
kept_facts.numeric_value: More than 1,000 candidate posts per person per day and thousands of signals, according to Meta's example description
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Meta's stated system-scale description, not an independently audited universal constant
kept_facts.source_title: How Does News Feed Predict What You Want to See? ([about.fb.com](https://about.fb.com/news/2021/01/how-does-news-feed-predict-what-you-want-to-see/?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The source is a company description and does not disclose the complete ranking model or all current signals.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Use this as evidence that ranking, not only user subscription, determines prominence. Avoid claiming that engagement is the sole objective.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Metaの公式説明は、News Feedが投稿の表示順をランキングし、フォロー、いいね、最近のエンゲージメントなどを含むシグナルから、ユーザーが関心を持つ・反応する確率を予測すると述べている。1ユーザー当たり1,000件超の候補投稿と数千のシグナルという規模の説明もある。ただし、これはMeta自身による説明であり、完全な現行モデルの開示ではない。([about.fb.com](https://about.fb.com/news/2021/01/how-does-news-feed-predict-what-you-want-to-see/))

kept_facts.claim: A Reuters Institute survey across 27 markets found that close to half of respondents were comfortable with automated selection of news based on previous preferences, although comfort with personalization was lower for news than for weather, music, and online television.
kept_facts.subject: Public comfort with personalized news selection
kept_facts.conditions: The measure concerns comfort with websites or apps automatically selecting content based on previous preferences.
kept_facts.numeric_value: 27 markets; close to half of respondents
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Market count and approximate share of survey respondents
kept_facts.source_title: How audiences think about news personalisation in the AI era ([reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2025/how-audiences-think-about-news-personalisation-ai-era))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The page text gives an approximate share rather than the exact percentage; the chart's underlying numerical values are not reproduced in the text.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Treat this as reported comfort, not proof that personalization improves news outcomes.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Reuters Instituteの2025年調査ページは、27市場で調査し、ニュースの自動パーソナライズに「快適」と答えた回答者が「close to half」で、天気・音楽・オンラインテレビなどより低かったと報告している。([reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2025/how-audiences-think-about-news-personalisation-ai-era))

kept_facts.claim: In open-ended responses analyzed by the Reuters Institute, people who were comfortable with personalized news commonly described it as more relevant to their lives and more efficient because it helped them avoid uninteresting topics or time spent viewing everything.
kept_facts.subject: Perceived convenience and relevance
kept_facts.scope: Open-ended comments from a subset of countries within the Reuters Institute study
kept_facts.conditions: These are respondents' reported perceptions, not experimentally measured time savings or comprehension gains.
kept_facts.source_title: How audiences think about news personalisation in the AI era ([reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2025/how-audiences-think-about-news-personalisation-ai-era))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The exact number of open-ended respondents and countries in this subset is not stated on the cited page.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Use 'respondents described' or 'perceived' rather than claiming measured time savings.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 同じReuters Instituteの分析は、パーソナライズに肯定的な回答者が、ニュースが自分の生活により関連し、興味のない話題を避けたり、すべてを見る時間を省けたりするため効率的だと説明したと記載している。これは回答者の認識であり、実測された時間短縮や理解度の因果効果ではないというLedgerの条件も妥当である。([reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2025/how-audiences-think-about-news-personalisation-ai-era))

kept_facts.claim: In the United States portion of the Reuters Institute's 2016 survey, 37% said automatically selecting stories based on their own past consumption was a good way to get news, compared with 22% for selection by editors and journalists and 17% for selection based on friends' consumption.
kept_facts.subject: Preference for selection method
kept_facts.scope: United States respondents; the report also covered 26 countries overall
kept_facts.conditions: The question asked respondents to rate each selection method as a good way to get news.
kept_facts.numeric_scope: United States respondents: past-consumption personalization; editors/journalists; friends' consumption, respectively
kept_facts.source_title: People Want Personalised Recommendations (Even as They Worry about the Consequences) ([reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/archive/essays/2016/people-want-personalised-recommendations/))
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This is a stated preference measure from 2016, not a measure of actual usage or news quality.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Reuters Instituteの2016年ページの米国表は、編集者・ジャーナリストによる選択22%、過去の自分の消費に基づく自動選択37%、友人の消費に基づく自動選択17%を示している。26か国調査の一部としての米国回答であり、実際の利用や品質の測定ではない。([reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/archive/essays/2016/people-want-personalised-recommendations/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: In the United States portion of the Reuters Institute's 2016 survey, 60% said they worried personalized news could cause them to miss important information, 59% worried about missing challenging viewpoints, and 49% worried about greater privacy risk.
kept_facts.subject: Reported concerns about personalization
kept_facts.scope: United States respondents; the report covered 26 countries overall
kept_facts.conditions: The question asked whether respondents were concerned about specific possible consequences of more personalized news.
kept_facts.numeric_scope: United States respondents: missing important information; missing challenging viewpoints; privacy risk, respectively
kept_facts.source_title: People Want Personalised Recommendations (Even as They Worry about the Consequences) ([reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/archive/essays/2016/people-want-personalised-recommendations/))
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: The same survey records both support for personalized selection and concern about its consequences.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 同じ2016年Reuters Instituteページの米国表は、重要情報の見落としへの懸念60%、異なる視点の見落としへの懸念59%、プライバシーリスクへの懸念49%を示している。([reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk](https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/archive/essays/2016/people-want-personalised-recommendations/?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: A study of browsing histories from 50,000 U.S.-located regular online-news users found that use of social networks and search engines was associated with greater mean ideological distance between individuals, while also being associated with greater exposure to material from each individual's less-preferred political side.
kept_facts.subject: Ideological diversity and segregation in online news use
kept_facts.scope: 50,000 U.S.-located users who regularly read online news
kept_facts.conditions: The findings are observational associations across consumption channels; they do not establish that personalization alone caused the differences.
kept_facts.source_title: Filter Bubbles, Echo Chambers, and Online News Consumption ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.2363701?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The study examines channels including social networks and web search; it does not isolate every individual platform's personalization system.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This fact supports both greater ideological separation across users and some increased exposure to opposing material; do not reduce it to a one-direction filter-bubble finding.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Flaxman・Goel・Raoの研究は、オンラインニュースを定期的に読む米国所在ユーザー5万人の閲覧履歴を分析し、ソーシャルネットワークと検索エンジンが個人間の平均的なイデオロギー距離の増加と関連し、同時に各人が好まない側の政治的内容への接触増加とも関連したと報告している。研究は観察的で、パーソナライズ単独の因果効果を識別していない。([5harad.com](https://5harad.com/papers/bubbles.pdf))

kept_facts.claim: The same 2016 browsing-history study reported that most online-news consumption consisted of users directly visiting the homepages of their favorite, typically mainstream, news outlets, which the authors said tempered both the positive and negative consequences of social networks and search engines; the reported effects were relatively modest.
kept_facts.subject: Overall composition of online news consumption
kept_facts.conditions: The claim concerns the study sample and its measured browsing behavior.
kept_facts.source_title: Filter Bubbles, Echo Chambers, and Online News Consumption ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.2363701?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Avoid implying that social feeds or search engines account for all online news exposure.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 同研究は、オンラインニュース消費の大部分が、ユーザーが主に主流派の好みのニュース媒体のホームページを直接訪問する形で生じており、そのためソーシャルネットワークと検索の正負両面の影響が弱められると述べ、効果の規模も比較的控えめだと報告している。([5harad.com](https://5harad.com/papers/bubbles.pdf))

kept_facts.claim: A study of 10.1 million U.S. Facebook users found that Facebook's algorithmically ranked News Feed reduced exposure to ideologically cross-cutting news relative to the content shared by users' friends, but users' own choices about what to click reduced such exposure more than algorithmic ranking did.
kept_facts.subject: Algorithmic ranking versus user choice
kept_facts.scope: 10.1 million U.S. Facebook users who interacted with socially shared news
kept_facts.conditions: The study measured exposure and clicks in an observational dataset; it did not randomly assign users to different ranking systems.
kept_facts.source_title: Exposure to ideologically diverse news and opinion on Facebook ([doi.org](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaa1160?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The study's results concern the Facebook environment and the period observed; they do not establish that user choice always dominates algorithmic effects on every platform.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This is evidence against a purely algorithm-driven explanation, not evidence that algorithmic ranking has no effect.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Bakshy・Messing・AdamicのScience研究は、米国Facebookユーザー1,010万人を分析し、アルゴリズムによるNews Feedランキングにより、友人が共有した内容に比べてクロスカッティングなニュースへの接触が減り、さらにユーザー自身のクリック選択の方がその接触を制限する役割が大きかったと報告している。([peeref.com](https://www.peeref.com/works/1357094?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: During the 2020 U.S. presidential election, content from politically like-minded sources constituted a majority of what active adult Facebook users saw, although political information and news made up only a small fraction of total exposures.
kept_facts.subject: Prevalence of like-minded exposure
kept_facts.scope: Entire population of active adult Facebook users in the United States, according to the study's platform-level analysis
kept_facts.conditions: The claim concerns source alignment across all types of Facebook content, not only news articles.
kept_facts.source_title: Like-minded sources on Facebook are prevalent but not polarizing ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06297-w?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The cited abstract does not give the exact majority percentage for the platform-level population analysis.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Distinguish 'like-minded sources' across Facebook content from political news specifically.
kept_facts.verification_notes: 2020年米大統領選期のFacebook研究について、大学側の研究概要は、米国のアクティブな成人Facebookユーザー全体を対象とした分析で、政治的に同類のソースからのコンテンツがユーザーが見る内容の多数を占めた一方、政治情報・ニュースは全露出の小さな割合だったと説明している。ここでいう露出はニュース記事だけでなくFacebook上のコンテンツ全般である。([asc.upenn.edu](https://www.asc.upenn.edu/news-events/news/first-findings-us-2020-facebook-instagram-election-study-released?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: In a field experiment involving 23,377 U.S.-based adult Facebook users, reducing exposure to content from like-minded sources from an average of 53.7% in the control group to 36.2% in the treatment group increased exposure to cross-cutting sources and reduced exposure to uncivil content, but produced no measurable effect on preregistered political attitudes such as affective polarization, ideological extremity, candidate evaluations, and belief in false claims.
kept_facts.subject: Experimental effect of reducing like-minded exposure
kept_facts.scope: 23,377 consenting U.S.-based adult Facebook users during the 2020 presidential election
kept_facts.conditions: Treatment downranked content of any type from friends, groups, and Pages predicted to share the participant's political leaning.
kept_facts.numeric_value: 23,377 users; 53.7% control exposure; 36.2% treatment exposure; approximately one-third reduction
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Experiment sample and average share of views from like-minded sources during the treatment period
kept_facts.source_title: Like-minded sources on Facebook are prevalent but not polarizing ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06297-w?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The experiment lasted about three months and studied existing Facebook users; it does not estimate effects of first exposure or cumulative exposure over many years.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Use the null result only for the measured period and outcomes; do not write that like-minded exposure can never affect attitudes.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Nature研究および関連する研究概要は、23,377人の米国成人Facebookユーザーを対象に、同類ソースからの露出を約3分の1減らす実験を行い、対照群53.7%に対し処置群36.2%だったこと、クロスカッティングなソースへの接触増加と非礼な内容への接触減少、ならびに事前登録した政治的態度指標への測定可能な効果がなかったことを報告している。([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06297-w?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: In a two-wave study during the 2018 and 2020 U.S. elections, participants engaged with more identity-congruent and unreliable news sources through Google Search than they were exposed to in their search results; the authors concluded that user choices, rather than algorithmic curation, were the primary driver of these differences in the study.
kept_facts.subject: Exposure versus engagement on Google Search
kept_facts.scope: Participants in a two-wave study combining surveys with ecologically measured Google Search exposure and engagement
kept_facts.conditions: The study compared URLs shown in search results with URLs selected by users; it did not treat all exposure as consumption.
kept_facts.source_title: Users choose to engage with more partisan news than they are exposed to on Google Search ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06078-5?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The findings concern Google Search during two U.S. election periods and should not be generalized automatically to social feeds or non-election periods.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This fact qualifies filter-bubble claims by separating what a system shows from what users choose to open.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Google Searchを対象にしたNature研究は、2018年・2020年米国選挙期の2波調査で、参加者が検索結果で露出したものよりも、アイデンティティ整合的で信頼性の低いニュースを多く選択してエンゲージしたと報告し、アルゴリズムによるキュレーションよりユーザーの選択が主な要因だと結論づけている。露出とクリック・閲覧などのエンゲージメントを区別するLedgerの条件も妥当である。([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06078-5?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: In a 2020-election experiment, assigning Facebook and Instagram users to reverse-chronological feeds instead of default algorithmic feeds substantially reduced time spent and activity on the platforms, increased exposure to political and untrustworthy content on both platforms, and did not significantly change issue polarization, affective polarization, political knowledge, or other key attitudes during the three-month study period.
kept_facts.subject: Effects of replacing algorithmic feeds with chronological feeds
kept_facts.scope: Consenting Facebook and Instagram users assigned to reverse-chronological feeds
kept_facts.conditions: The treatment replaced the default algorithmic ordering with reverse chronology; outcomes were measured during the study period.
kept_facts.source_title: How do social media feed algorithms affect attitudes and behavior in an election campaign? ([networkscienceinstitute.org](https://www.networkscienceinstitute.org/publications/how-do-social-media-feed-algorithms-affect-attitudes-and-behavior-in-an-election-campaign))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The source page does not state the full sample size; the null effects are limited to the measured outcomes and study period.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: The experiment shows that large changes in exposure and engagement can coexist with no detectable short-run change in measured political attitudes.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Science論文のPubMed要約は、2020年米国選挙でFacebookとInstagramの同意ユーザーを逆時系列フィードに割り当て、アルゴリズムフィードから移すと利用時間と活動が大きく減少し、政治的・信頼性の低い内容への露出が両プラットフォームで増加したと報告している。一方、3か月の期間中、争点・感情的分極、政治知識などの主要態度には有意な変化がなかった。([pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37498999/))

kept_facts.claim: An independent 2023 field experiment on X assigned active U.S. users to algorithmic or chronological feeds for an average of about seven weeks; switching from chronological to algorithmic increased engagement and shifted policy and current-political-news attitudes in a more conservative direction, while producing no significant change in affective polarization or self-reported partisanship.
kept_facts.subject: Political effects of X's algorithmic feed
kept_facts.date_or_period: July to September 2023 experiment; published February 18, 2026
kept_facts.scope: 4,965 active U.S. X users who completed the main pre- and post-treatment surveys
kept_facts.conditions: Participants were randomly assigned to X's algorithmic For You feed or chronological Following feed; the experiment studied X's 2023 feed system.
kept_facts.numeric_value: 4,965 participants; approximately 7 weeks; +0.12 standard deviations on the aggregated policy/current-political-news index for the chronological-to-algorithmic switch
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Main completed sample, average treatment duration, and reported composite outcome
kept_facts.source_title: The political effects of X's feed algorithm ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10098-2?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The result is platform-, country-, period-, and algorithm-specific; the paper cautions that it may not generalize to algorithms that amplify both ideological sides similarly.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: This is evidence that effects can differ by platform and direction of switching. Do not present it as a universal effect of all personalization.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Nature掲載論文は、2023年に米国のアクティブなXユーザーを7週間、アルゴリズムフィードまたは時系列フィードへ無作為割付し、4,965人が事後調査を完了したと記載している。時系列からアルゴリズムへの切替はエンゲージメントを増やし、政策優先順位・トランプ捜査・ウクライナ戦争に関する態度を保守方向へ動かした一方、感情的分極と自己申告の党派性には有意な効果がなかった。政策・政治ニュース統合指標の効果は0.12標準偏差である。([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10098-2?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: A Congressional Research Service report states that social-media operators use algorithms based on user behavior and revealed preferences, including clicks, likes, shares, and search history, and can tune these systems toward business goals such as maximizing engagement and advertising revenue.
kept_facts.subject: Commercial and behavioral incentives in algorithmic ranking
kept_facts.date_or_period: Congressional Research Service report accessed September 14, 2026
kept_facts.scope: Social-media content dissemination systems generally; not a finding about one named platform's current algorithm
kept_facts.conditions: The report describes common platform practices and incentives, not a universal rule for every service.
kept_facts.source_title: Social Media: Content Dissemination and Moderation Practices ([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/PDF/R46662/R46662.7.pdf?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.ambiguity: The report summarizes documented industry practices; it does not establish that every ranking decision is driven primarily by commercial incentives.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Use 'can be tuned toward' or 'are described as pursuing' rather than claiming that commercial incentives always override editorial or public-interest goals.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Congressional Research Serviceは、ソーシャルメディア事業者がプロフィール、クリック、いいね、シェア、検索履歴などのオンライン行動・顕示選好に基づくアルゴリズムを使い、エンゲージメントや広告収益の最大化などの事業目標に合わせて調整できると説明している。全サービスに常に同じ優先目的があるという主張ではないというLedgerの限定も適切である。([congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/PDF/R46662/R46662.7.pdf?utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: Under Article 27 of the EU Digital Services Act, online platforms using recommender systems must explain the main parameters used and the options users have to modify or influence them; under Article 38, very large online platforms and very large online search engines must provide at least one recommender-system option that is not based on profiling.
kept_facts.subject: Legal transparency and non-profiling alternatives
kept_facts.date_or_period: Digital Services Act Regulation (EU) 2022/2065; applicable legal framework accessed September 14, 2026
kept_facts.scope: Online platforms using recommender systems under Article 27; very large online platforms and very large online search engines under Article 38
kept_facts.conditions: Article 38's non-profiling alternative applies to designated very large online platforms and very large online search engines, not every app or website.
kept_facts.ambiguity: The regulation creates transparency and choice obligations; it does not itself establish that the resulting systems are unbiased or that users will select non-profiled options.
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Use as evidence that policymakers treat recommender-system parameters and profiling as governance issues, not as proof that transparency solves the underlying risks.
kept_facts.verification_notes: EUデジタルサービス法第27条は、レコメンダーシステムを使うオンラインプラットフォームに、主なパラメータと利用者がそれを変更・影響できる選択肢の説明を求めている。第38条は、非常に大規模なオンラインプラットフォームおよび非常に大規模なオンライン検索エンジンに、各レコメンダーシステムについてプロファイリングに基づかない選択肢を少なくとも1つ提供するよう求める。Ledgerの適用範囲の限定は正しい。([eur-lex.europa.eu](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2022/2065/oj?eliuri=eli%3Areg%3A2022%3A2065%3Aoj&locale=en&utm_source=openai))

kept_facts.claim: The Nature study on reducing like-minded Facebook exposure explicitly states that its design could not capture effects of prior Facebook use or cumulative exposure over years, and that longer experiments or studies among new users would be needed to assess those possibilities.
kept_facts.subject: Limits of short-run experimental evidence
kept_facts.scope: 23,377 U.S. adult Facebook users in the intervention study
kept_facts.conditions: The limitation applies to interpreting the study's null effects on political attitudes.
kept_facts.numeric_value: Three-month intervention; cumulative exposure over years not measured
kept_facts.numeric_scope: Study duration and unmeasured longer-term period
kept_facts.source_title: Like-minded sources on Facebook are prevalent but not polarizing ([nature.com](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06297-w?utm_source=openai))
kept_facts.notes_for_writer: Do not convert a short-run null result into a claim that worldview narrowing over long periods has been ruled out.
kept_facts.verification_notes: Nature論文は、実験設計では過去のFacebook利用や数年にわたる累積露出の効果を捉えられず、より長期の実験や新規ユーザーを対象とする研究が必要だと明記している。したがって、3か月の短期的な政治態度の無効果を長期的な世界観の狭窄が存在しないことへ一般化しないという注記は妥当である。([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/10396953/?utm_source=openai))
